The use of words does not automatically mean that data is qualitative. When the data being collected is in word form, but the intention is to count the number of each answer, then it is not qualitative. Examples would include when questions only have a very limited number of answers, e.g. asking ‘is this surprise?’ (i.e. answers = yes/no) or having a number of emotions that need to be identified by name, but with the intention that the number of answers for each one are then counted.
